column3: Pairs the human subject with self-witness, sharpening the motive attributed in 75:5.
Its stabilizing sacred center is only a distant contrast to a human wish to overrun what lies ahead.
Relates wanting the immediate to a bounded, not self-controlled, outcome; a secondary frame for desire in 75:5.
Another bal-yuridu construction presents desire as a demand to control the terms of reception, while its exploratory reading remains secondary.
The nearby forward/backward accounting gives concrete temporal scope to what the human wants before him.
Contrasts self-interested wanting with action refusing return or thanks, clarifying a non-acquisitive direction of desire.
Sets divine intending to ease alongside human weakness, contrasting the human desire in 75:5 with another intentional relation.
The immediately preceding assertion of capacity over fingertips counters any unrestricted human projection into the future.
Opposes divine will for repentance to desire-followers wanting a great deviation, closely illuminating a transgressive intended course.
Presents an agent whose willing is effective, contrasting human wanting with sovereign enactment.
The threat of being swallowed without awareness supplies only a remote consequence-side contrast to transgression ahead.
Its reversal of ordinary familial orientation is a distant spatial parallel, not evidence for 75:5's forward desire.

The moon's eclipse belongs to the same nearby upheaval sequence, framing the future that cannot be mastered.
Names the fujjar and their consequence, directly supplying the moral category evoked by liyafjura.

Links intended plotting to its recoil upon unbelievers, offering a related pattern of harmful purpose turned back.
Following ancestral traces is a possible inherited-direction contrast, but it does not address fujur directly.

Controlled springs in gardens give only a distant, contrary image of ordered opening rather than transgression.

The weighing of deeds is a later evaluative frame, without a direct link to the desire in 75:5.
Contrasts desire aimed at the hereafter with desire aimed at the world, making temporal orientation central to wanting.
Human ingratitude toward the Lord provides a related moral disposition, though not the forward temporal element.
The nearby expectation of a crushing event counters the human's presumed license before him.
The abyss as a destination is a loose orientation parallel; its desire/direction reading is secondary.
Calls the human to examine provision, countering unreflective self-directed pursuit with attention to dependence.
Avoidance of major sins and indecencies supplies an explicit moral contrary to fujur, with humility about the self.
Acknowledges possible deceptive intent while refusing to let suspicion erase a stated course, a limited contrast in reading intentions.
Condemns the human's extreme ingratitude, reinforcing the moral diagnosis around 75:5.
The flashing sight is part of the immediate scene that interrupts the human's imagined forward freedom.
Treats demanded bursting water as a condition imposed on faith, paralleling desire that tries to set its own terms.
The human's loss supplies a broad outcome-frame for a course of continuing transgression.
Calling the human to consider origin counters autonomous self-projection, though indirectly.

The belief that wealth makes one lasting exposes a false future-security analogous to unchecked forward projection.

Stone opening and water emerging offer a figurative breach contrast, but no clear human desire or fujur link.
Depicts divine will becoming reality without delay, contrasting human intention with effective creative command.
Follows conjecture and soul-desire against guidance, a close alternative account of desire misdirecting conduct.

Human creation from a clinging origin provides a broad corrective to self-exalting transgression.
Guardianship over every soul is a general accountability theme, only indirectly relevant.

Someone coming earnestly supplies only a loose forward-movement contrast.

Ordered spring distribution and prohibition of corruption are a distant social contrast to fujur.

Questioning can become a turn from faith to disbelief, a parallel for desire becoming a path of deviation.
Human learning of what was unknown counters self-sufficient claims, indirectly bearing on the human subject.
Explicitly distinguishes reformers and the muttaqun from corrupters and fujjar, clarifying the moral alternative.
The human's startled question at upheaval belongs to a general eschatological frame, not the motive itself.
An evident road as public warning is only a remote orientation image.
The demanded garden and rivers extend the self-serving sign-demand pattern, though only analogically.
Wanting God, the Messenger, and the hereafter presents a contrary object and obligation for desire.
Channeling a spring to others is a distant controlled-flow contrast to fujur's breach imagery.

Worldly wealth and children as punishment give a remote warning about desired worldly goods.
Affirms that God does what He wills amid human conflict, contrasting sovereign will with human divergence.
Explicitly contrasts those wanting the world and those wanting the hereafter, tying desire to conduct and testing.
Questions the wanting of false gods, presenting desire as a choice that can depart from truth.
Attributes a purpose of enmity, hatred, and diversion to Satan, supplying a social consequence-side reading of harmful intent.
Its blocked-path discussion concerns attempted guidance, only distantly related to intended direction.
Wanting worldly life and adornment gives a direct temporal horizon parallel, despite a different stated outcome.

Unravelling a strong weave is a figurative breaking contrast, not a direct reading of fujur ahead.
Sudden inescapable arrival supplies only a general contrary to postponement or escape.
Seeking ruin of places of worship is a harmful undertaking, but lacks a close lexical or temporal link.
Taking near worldly gain while expecting forgiveness models repeated moral opportunism across a future course.
Knowledge of what is before and behind humans provides a remote frame for 'before him,' without explaining fujur.
An alleged intent toward evil is contested within a scene, offering only a loose intention parallel.
False gods disappearing from their devotees is a broad consequence of invented devotion, not a close link.
Contrasts a woman's desire for chastity with coercion for worldly gain, preserving opposed desires around sexual transgression.

The joining of sun and moon is part of the same immediate endpoint that interrupts human forward projection.
The immediate denial of any refuge directly counters an imagined ability to keep escaping ahead.
Self-testimony despite excuses extends 75:14's self-witness and exposes the human's self-account.

The contrast between wanting worldly gain and God's wanting the hereafter is a direct alternative to 75:5's forward desire.

The intent to extinguish God's light shows harmful purpose directed against disclosed guidance.

Taking hawa as a god presents an intensified account of desire becoming governing allegiance.
Divine intent to remove defilement offers a moral contrary to the human wish for fujur.
The prohibition against following hawa frames desire as a force that can divert from God's path.
Taking hawa as a god, alongside knowledge and sealing, closely sharpens the self-authorizing dimension of 75:5.
The laggards' wish to follow later and alter God's word illustrates desire seeking to revise a fixed future judgment.
Turning away while wanting only worldly life supplies a direct temporal-object parallel to 75:5.
Naming the one who tagha gives a close moral parallel to the human's intended fujur.

Jahim as the shelter states the consequence paired with tagha and worldly preference in the preceding lines.
Willing to be upright provides a positive use of human willing, without resolving its relation to divine will.
The following qualification by divine willing preserves the asymmetry between human volition and sovereign will.
Preferring worldly life supplies a concise alternative formulation of a near-horizon desire.
The better and more lasting hereafter supplies the contrary horizon to worldly preference.
Being diverted by hope while consuming present enjoyment closely illuminates a future-facing disposition that defers reckoning.
The human's haste in calling for evil relates urgency and harmful orientation, though not fujur explicitly.
Human creation from haste provides a disposition-level parallel to pursuing an unchecked course ahead.
Human restlessness offers a broader character frame for the self-directed instability implied in 75:5.
Intense love of wealth gives a concrete worldly attachment that may supply one motive for continuing excess.
Rival accumulation distracting until graves presents an extended temporal course of worldly preoccupation.
